*AI Safety Asia is looking for Head of Frontier AI Risk!* Sharing more from them below:

We're looking for someone who operates at the intersection of technical depth and policy practice: fluent in evaluations and their limits, safety cases, agentic systems and loss-of-control risk, compute and supply-chain governance, and misuse pathways — and equally fluent in turning that into option papers that ministers, regulators and AI safety institute leadership across Asia can act on.
It's a rare combination, and we know the right person may not be actively looking.

*Full job description and how to apply:* <https://lnkd.in/g_vCCfKV|lnkd.in/g_vCCfKV>

*<https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/miri/5d13ba07-8fbf-4f46-aa1b-9000a7d1dc3f|MIRI is hiring Policy Advisors> to help us build our DC policy efforts*
MIRI is a nonprofit that has been working on avoiding catastrophic outcomes from advanced AI for over 20 years. After doing technical research for much of that time, MIRI pivoted to focusing on raising awareness of the threat and identifying policy responses. Now, the danger seems close. We’re aiming to significantly ramp up our engagement with the U.S. Federal Government in the coming weeks, as we see major gaps and opportunities. There is movement on serious AI policy, including growing support for a ban on superintelligence, yet much more work is needed.

What we’re hiring for:
• People with a *strong background in government or a proven track record at advocating for policy changes*. We are most excited about mid-to-senior level folks but may hire a couple of junior people. 
• Specific tasks for a Policy Advisor could include: Brief government offices, Network in the AI policy community, Provide feedback on draft legislation, and Do the full stack of AI policy research. 
• Applicants do not need to agree with “the MIRI worldview” about everything. They should be comfortable working toward MIRI’s mission. 
• Pay range is $120k–$300k. Location is DC (strongly preferred). Can sponsor visas for exceptional candidates. 
What sets MIRI apart from other AI policy orgs:
• We are direct and honest about our concern that <https://intelligence.org/the-problem/|superintelligent AI might cause human extinction>. We think that outcome is likely (and soon) on the current trajectory. 
• We think the only survivable solution is to buy more time: a global prohibition on superintelligence. See <https://intelligence.org/agreementshort|this 1-pager>. Corollary: many other policies are ineffective and we say so. 
• We do research on what policies would Actually Work™ and then push for these policies to happen. We don’t nibble at the problem, we try to win. 
• Is this an impactful role? We’ve had some success already and we think the tide is moving in our favor: the world is starting to realize that ASI is an extinction threat, and we are one of the only groups that has been saying that for years (and figuring out the policy solutions). 
_This is an open hiring round, and we would appreciate you sharing this with anybody who you think might be a good fit! Applications are rolling, but the world is running out of time. <https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/miri/5d13ba07-8fbf-4f46-aa1b-9000a7d1dc3f|Apply here>._
